question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendments — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of this bill, which became a stopgap that funds federal agencies into fiscal year 2027, generally through December 11, 2026, and extends several expiring programs. It is not a vote on the bill's original Africa-trade text. A two-thirds Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036 (H CON RES 113)
bill_title: Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036.
plain_language: This resolution sets federal budget targets for fiscal year 2027 through 2036 and instructs several House committees to write bills that would raise the deficit by limited amounts, which can move under faster reconciliation rules. A Yea adopts that budget plan. A Nay rejects it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government (H J RES 139)
bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government.
plain_language: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment prohibiting total federal expenditures for a year from exceeding the average annual federal receipts collected in the three prior years, adjusted for changes in the population of U.S. citizens and inflation. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.
